Without it resid𝐄 was about \(10^{-4}\) for a conducting inner core turning with \(\Delta\Omega(r_i) eq 0\); with it the budget is the same in every frame.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: Each step of the port was checked when it was built: against conductive_IC, against exact and published solutions, term by term against a symbolic derivation, and with the energy budgets. The parts were ported from the conductive_IC branch (commit 39487bbf), formula by formula, into this branch's conventions: on 2026-10-28 insulating walls (step 1), a conducting inner core (step 2), any density profile (step 3), a toroidal background field (step 4), the full sphere, inviscid runs and the poloidal fields of degree 2 (step 5); on 2026-10-30 the induction by a differential rotation, a confined field, fields of any degrees and the Ferraro field, with couplings built from the recurrence algebra. The scripts are in tests/magnetic/ (run_all.sh).

docs.title: Against conductive_IC, insulating walls (2026-10-28)
docs.text:
Step 1 reproduces conductive_IC to round-off, for every eigenvalue and residual.

Spin-over geometry of the conductive_IC test: ricb 0.35, Ek 1e-3, no-slip walls (bci = bco = 1), N 68, lmax 64 (63 for m = 0), 2 ranks; \(\Lambda = 1\), Pm = 1 (Le \(= \sqrt{10^{-3}}\), Em \(= 10^{-3}\)), cnorm = 'mag_energy', insulating walls; conductive_IC at 39487bbf with the same parameters. All five eigenvalues of each run:

case target largest relative difference 'axial', m 1, symm −1 1.0i 8e-15 'FDM', m 1, symm −1 1.0i 7e-15 'axial', m 0, symm 1 0.3i 1e-13 'FDM', m 0, symm 1 0.3i 9e-14

The least damped m = 1 mode: λ = −0.104550975908 + 1.009269490234i ('axial'), −0.104198820746 + 1.008910499350i ('FDM'). residσ and resid𝐛 agree with conductive_IC's resid𝐮 and resid𝐛 mode by mode (1e-15 to 1e-10). Without the field (magnetic = 0, structure 'Boussinesq', no-slip) the hydrodynamic spin-over is λ = −0.1019947097 + 1.0057336901i, the conductive_IC reference. Non-magnetic matrices are bitwise unchanged (tests/diff_rot/regress.sh).

docs.title: Conducting inner core (2026-10-28)
docs.text:
Step 2 reproduces conductive_IC with a conducting inner core to round-off, residuals included.

FDM (\(l = 1\)), cnorm = 'Schmitt2012', ricb 0.35, Ek \(10^{-5}\), \(\Lambda = 10\), Pm 0.1, no-slip walls, insulating mantle, conducting inner core, 4 ranks, the same parameters in conductive_IC (39487bbf). The m = 0 target is the most torsional of the modes there at this resolution (ω 0.0747, σ −0.0233, 𝒯/𝒫 18, Geo 0.90).

case N, lmax largest relative difference (5 eigenvalues) m 0, \(\sigma_{i2o} = \mu_{i2o} = 1\), N_cic 64 80, 79 2e-13 m 1 (target 1.0i) 80, 80 4e-14 m 0 128, 127 6e-13 m 1 128, 128 1e-14 m 0, \(\sigma_{i2o} = 10^{-2}\) 80, 79 3e-13 m 0, N_cic 48 / 96 80, 79 3e-13 / 2e-13 m 0, \(\mu_{i2o} = 2\) 80, 79 2e-13 m 1, \(\mu_{i2o} = 2\), \(\sigma_{i2o} = 0.3\) 80, 80 7e-14

The least damped m = 0 mode: λ = −0.023322278633 + 0.074686068661i (N 80), −0.023322202914 + 0.074686566522i (N 128). residσ, resid𝐛 and resid𝐄 equal conductive_IC's resid𝐮, resid𝐛, resid𝐄 to the printed digits (resid𝐄 with \(\mu_{i2o} \ne 1\) apart, see Energy budgets). N 80 is not enough at Ek \(10^{-5}\): residuals \(10^{-6}\) to \(10^{-3}\), \(10^{-14}\) to \(10^{-6}\) at N 128. N_cic 48, 64 and 96 give the same eigenvalues to \(2\cdot10^{-14}\). At Ek \(10^{-3}\) (the geometry above, \(\Lambda\) = Pm = 1) 'axial' m 1 and 'FDM' m 0 agree to \(3\cdot10^{-13}\), with all residuals below \(10^{-10}\).

docs.title: Variable density checks (2026-10-28)
docs.text:
No other code has the terms of step 3, so they were checked five ways: against their derivation, with operator identities, row by row, with the energy budgets, and by continuity towards a uniform density. The scripts are in tests/magnetic/ (run_all.sh), with bin/ru_insane.py:

  • Derivation. The rows derived from the definitions reproduce conductive_IC's 44 uniform-density blocks exactly (factor −1, the A sign; l 3–6, m 0–3), and the \((\ln\rho_0)'\) terms equal the closed forms of Variable density to \(\le 2\cdot10^{-14}\); the rows v and the T columns have none. The closed forms are those of the planning notes: none had to be corrected.
  • Uniform density unchanged. The 4 insulating and 9 conducting-core cases above give A and B bitwise equal to the code before this step.
  • Operator identities (bin/ru_insane.py, B0 'axial', no-slip): \(\int\rho_0\mathbf u^*\cdot\mathbf F_L\,dV = -\mathrm{Hendrik}\,\overline{\int\mathbf b^*\cdot\nabla\times(\mathbf u\times\mathbf B_0)\,dV}\) to \(5\cdot10^{-15}\) ('Boussinesq') and \(1\cdot10^{-10}\) ('Wu 2005', r_out 0.99, N 96; \(7\cdot10^{-13}\) at N 160), m 0, 1, 2; switching off the g-row or the u-row terms gives \(2\cdot10^{-3}\) and 0.2. b block Hermitian positive and diffusion Hermitian negative to \(10^{-14}\).
  • Row checks (row_check.py, 'Wu 2005', N 192): every magnetic row block against the derivation, unweighted, to \(10^{-14}\) ('axial' m 1, 'FDM' m 0 with tol_B0 = 1e-15; \(8\cdot10^{-9}\) with the default tol_B0 = 1e-8, the cut of the B0 series). At N 96 the blocks with \(\lambda_1\) are good to \(10^{-7}\) only: the series of \((\ln\rho_0)'\) converge slowly, its pole sits at \(r = 1/r_\mathrm{out}\).

  • Energy budgets ('Wu 2005', r_out 0.99, ricb 0.35, FDM, conducting inner core, no-slip, \(\Lambda\) = Pm = 1). At Ek \(10^{-3}\), residσ, residω, resid𝐛 and resid𝐄 for m 0 and m 1 are \(10^{-3}\) at N 68, \(10^{-7}\) at N 128 and \(\le 6\cdot10^{-10}\) at N 192. At Ek \(10^{-4}\) (all residuals \(\le 3\cdot10^{-9}\) at N 256):

    mode λ (N 256) change least damped, m 1 −0.005739718 + 1.003574886i \(3\cdot10^{-9}\) at N 192, \(10^{-8}\) with lmax 96 instead of 64 m 0, near 0.0442i −0.017420795 + 0.044242829i

    The budgets use spin_doctor's own Lorentz and induction formulas, so they check the rows independently; the f and g rows need no \(\rho_0\) weight, although \(\lambda_1 \approx -200\) at the outer wall.

  • Continuity ('Wu 2005' with r_out = \(\sqrt\epsilon\), so the stratification is \(O(\epsilon)\), against 'Boussinesq'; axial, m 1, Ek \(10^{-3}\), N 96): the eigenvalue moves linearly with the stratification.

    \(\epsilon\) \(10^{-4}\) \(10^{-3}\) \(10^{-2}\) \(10^{-1}\) (λ − λ of 'Boussinesq')/ε 0.05186 − 0.00053i 0.05188 0.05215 0.05498

docs.title: Toroidal field (2026-10-28)
docs.text:
Step 4 was checked against its derivation, with the energy budgets, and against the exact frequencies of the Malkus (1967) field.

  • Derivation. The closed forms equal derive.py's rows (\(b_0\) = ('tor', 1) and ('tor', 2), any \(\rho_0\)) for l 3–6, m 0–3 (derive_check.py); every coefficient fitted from l 2–9, m 0–3 (n = 1) and l 3–9 (n = 2), exactly.
  • Earlier cases unchanged. The 13 cases of steps 1 and 2 and three 'Wu 2005' cases of step 3 give A and B bitwise equal to the code before this step.
  • Row checks ('Wu 2005', N 192): 'Malkus' m 1 to \(10^{-14}\); 'wall' m 0, 2 to \(2\cdot10^{-10}\), in the u-row blocks with \(k\lambda_1\) only (they vanish at the wall, where \(\lambda_1\) is large, so the relative error of the near-wall \(\lambda_1\) series shows; it does not decrease with N).
  • Energy budgets. 'Malkus' and 'wall', 'Boussinesq' (N 68, 96) and 'Wu 2005' (N 128, 192), insulating and conducting inner core, m 0 and 1, Ek = Em = \(10^{-3}\), \(\mathrm{Le}^2 = 10^{-3}\), cnorm_tor = 'mag_energy': residσ, resid𝐛, resid𝐄 \(\le 6\cdot10^{-13}\), eigenvalues the same at both N to the printed digits. Unlike a poloidal field, the toroidal one has no radial component, hence no Hartmann layer at the walls, and 'Wu 2005' converges fast.
  • Degree 2 and combined fields. 'Malkus' and 'wall' with B0_tor_l = 2, 'Boussinesq' (N 68, 96) and 'Wu 2005' (N 128, 192), conducting inner core, m 0 and 1: residuals \(\le 10^{-11}\), eigenvalues the same at both N to the printed digits. FDM plus a degree-2 'wall' field ('Wu 2005'): residuals \(2\cdot10^{-10}\) at N 192 (the poloidal field's Hartmann layer sets the resolution); row check of 'axial' plus a degree-2 'Malkus' field, m 2: \(10^{-14}\). A 'user' profile 'r' gives the 'Malkus' eigenvalues to \(10^{-12}\).

  • Malkus (1967). With \(B_\phi = \mathrm{Le}\,s\) the induction is \(im\,\mathrm{Le}\,\mathbf u\) and the Lorentz force, up to a gradient,

    \[ \mathbf F_L = \frac{im\,\mathrm{Le}^2}{\lambda}\left(im\,\mathbf u + 2\hat{\mathbf z}\times\mathbf u\right), \]

    so the ideal problem reduces to that of the inertial waves (frequency \(\lambda_\mathrm{in}\)) in any container:

    \[ \omega = \frac{\lambda_\mathrm{in}}{2}\left[1 \pm \sqrt{1 + \frac{4\mathrm{Le}^2 m(m - \lambda_\mathrm{in})}{\lambda_\mathrm{in}^2}}\right] \]

    (kore's Im of the eigenvalue; the spin-over, \(\lambda_\mathrm{in} = m = 1\), does not move). For small Le the shift divided by \(\mathrm{Le}^2\) tends to

    \[ \frac{m(m-\lambda_\mathrm{in})}{\lambda_\mathrm{in}} . \]

    For six m = 1 modes near 0.75i ('Boussinesq', ricb 0.35, Pm 1, insulating walls) the frequency shift is exactly quadratic in Le (the same shift divided by \(\mathrm{Le}^2\) for \(\mathrm{Le}^2\) = 1e-6, 4e-6 and 1.6e-5), and its distance to this limit falls with the diffusivities: 2–8 % at Ek = Em = \(10^{-5}\), 0.4–1 % at \(10^{-6}\) (e.g. 0.3808 against 0.3822 for \(\lambda_\mathrm{in}\) = 0.7235). tests/magnetic/malkus_check.py.

docs.title: Full sphere, inviscid runs and degree-2 poloidal fields
docs.text:
Step 5 (2026-10-28) was checked against the inviscid modes of Wu (2005) and of Luo & Jackson (2022), against conductive_IC, and with the energy budgets.

  • Hydrodynamics. Inviscid Boussinesq full sphere (Ek = 0, 'Boussinesq'): the inertial modes of Wu (2005, Table 1, β = 0) to the 10 digits given (e.g. 0.6666666667, 1.4964360838, 1.2319250547 for \(\lvert m\rvert = 2\)); 'Wu 2005' against its Table 2. No non-magnetic code changed (regress.sh bitwise).
  • Against conductive_IC (39487bbf, the geometry of the first check, all eigenvalues of each run): full sphere, 'axial', 'FDM' (\(l\) = 1, 2), 'G21 dipole', 'Luo_S1', 'Luo_S2', m 0–2 and both symmetries, \(\le 5\cdot10^{-13}\); with an inner core (insulating or conducting, B0_ic = 'potential'): 'G21 dipole', 'Luo_S1', 'Luo_S2', 'FDM' \(l = 2\) (m 0, 3), \(\le 6\cdot10^{-13}\).
  • Derivation. derive_check.py also checks the tables of induction_pol2, lorentz_pol2, read from operators.py, against derive.py's rows (l 3–6, m 0–3), to round-off.
  • Row checks in a full sphere (row_check.py handles the parity-reduced bases and \(\Delta l = \pm2\)): 'Boussinesq' to \(10^{-14}\); 'Wu 2005' needs N 288 (the pole of \((\ln\rho_0)'\) at \(r = 1/r_\mathrm{out}\) is nearer to the domain \([-1, 1]\) than to a shell's; \(3\cdot10^{-7}\) at N 192).

  • Energy budgets, 'Wu 2005', Ek = Em = \(10^{-3}\) ('Boussinesq': to \(10^{-14}\)):

    case N 128 N 192 N 256 'Luo_S2', full sphere, m 0 \(10^{-7}\) \(3\cdot10^{-11}\) 'Luo_S2', full sphere, m 1 \(3\cdot10^{-6}\) \(10^{-9}\) 'Luo_S2', insulating or conducting inner core \(10^{-10}\) FDM \(l = 2\), full sphere, 'Schmitt2012' (its Hartmann layer) \(5\cdot10^{-4}\) \(6\cdot10^{-6}\) \(3\cdot10^{-8}\)

  • Malkus (1967), ideal. Inviscid Boussinesq full sphere, \(B_\phi = \mathrm{Le}\,s\), Em \(10^{-9}\), m 2: for ten inertial modes \(\lambda_\mathrm{in}\) of both symmetries and Le 0.1, 0.3, both branches of the Malkus frequency above to \(10^{-5}\)–\(7\cdot10^{-3}\) relative at N 64 (the fast branch to \(10^{-4}\) at N 96). The error does not change with Em (\(10^{-8}\) to \(10^{-10}\)) or with Le: it is that of the magnetic boundary layer the insulating wall imposes (Malkus's ideal solution has a tangential \(\mathbf b\) there), not resolved at these N. Since 2026-11-07 an inviscid run with this field and an insulating mantle, where the field is not zero, stops (Current sheets at slipping walls).

  • Torsional modes of Luo & Jackson (2022) (conductive_IC's tests/torsional_s2: 'Luo_S2', inviscid, Lu \(2\cdot10^4\), m 0, timescale = 'Alfven'). This code converges to their modes as \(N^{-3}\):

    mode Luo & Jackson relative difference 1 −0.0065952461 + 1.0335959942i \(1.3\cdot10^{-5}\) (N 128), \(4\cdot10^{-7}\) (N 320) 2 −0.0141833345 + 1.9095123626i \(2\cdot10^{-4}\) (N 128), \(7\cdot10^{-6}\) (N 384)

    conductive_IC is within \(10^{-6}\) already at N 128 because it mishandles the \(D^3\) and \(D^2\) Lorentz terms (Rows and implementation, inviscid runs), whose effect there is only \(10^{-7}\): with its bases set as here it gives this code's eigenvalues to \(10^{-9}\). The slow convergence comes from the u rows in \(C^{(3)}\), where the unresolved boundary layer of \(\mathbf b\) (Em \(5\cdot10^{-9}\)) enters through \(f'''\).

docs.title: Differential rotation, confined, general and Ferraro fields (2026-10-30)
docs.text:
The induction by a differential rotation and the fields of any degrees were checked against sympy, against exact solutions (a rigid rotation, the uniform axial field, a closed-form wound field), and with the energy budgets; without the new features nothing changed.

  • ∇×(U0×b) against sympy (tests/magnetic/dr_induction_check.py): the blocks of diff_rot.induction_block against derive.rows_dr for \(n\) = 0–6, \(m\) = 0–5, \(l\) up to 25, term by term: \(\le 10^{-13}\) at low \(l\); at \(l\) 20–25 the agreement is limited by derive.py's own quadrature (\(10^{-10}\)).
  • Rigid rotation, exact (rigid_check.py): a uniform \(\Delta\Omega = c\) must give the eigenvalue of Gaspard \(1 + c\) without rotation, minus \(imc\). All eigenvalues agree to \(\le 5\cdot10^{-14}\): hydrodynamics, 'axial', 'FDM', 'Luo_S2', 'Malkus', 'wall' of degree 2, a conducting inner core, a full sphere.
  • Budgets with a solar-like \(\Delta\Omega = f_0 + f_2P_2 + f_4P_4\) (Ek = Em = \(10^{-3}\), \(\Lambda\) = 1): 'Malkus', 'axial' and 'Luo_S2', shell and full sphere, 'Boussinesq' and 'Wu 2005': residσ, resid𝐛, resid𝐄 \(10^{-13}\)–\(10^{-9}\).
  • The algebra against the closed forms (mag_couplings 'algebra' against 'closed', same runs): eigenvalues equal to \(\le 6\cdot10^{-13}\) for 'axial' (m 0, 1), 'FDM' (degree 2), 'Luo_S2' (shell, full sphere, 'Wu 2005'), 'FDM' with 'Wu 2005', 'Malkus' (and 'Wu 2005'), 'wall' of degree 2, 'axial' + 'wall', a conducting inner core, 'confined', and with a differential rotation. Against sympy (algebra_check.py): every block for poloidal and toroidal fields of degree 1–4 (3 and 4 have no closed forms), several \(m\), \(l\) up to 12.
  • 'general': \(h_1 = r/2\) gives exactly the 'axial' eigenvalues (no-slip walls: at a slipping insulating outer wall 'general' ends in a sheet, being taken as a field of currents in the fluid), \(k_1 = r\) exactly the 'Malkus' ones; fields of degrees 1 + 3 (full sphere), 2 + 4 (shell), toroidal 1 + 3, and a poloidal 1 + 3 with a toroidal 2 and a differential rotation (also 'Wu 2005'): budgets \(\le 5\cdot10^{-12}\).
  • 'confined': degree 1 and 2, shell layer [0.4, 0.8] and full-sphere layer [0, 0.6]: budgets \(10^{-12}\)–\(10^{-14}\) (shell), \(4\cdot10^{-10}\) (degree 1, N 192) and \(2\cdot10^{-9}\) (degree 2, N 384) in the full sphere; with \(\Delta\Omega\) uniform inside the layer, ferraro_mismatch = \(10^{-29}\) and the budgets close as without rotation.
  • 'ferraro': with a cylindrical rotation and \(G(w) = w\) the field is the uniform axial one, and the eigenvalues equal those of 'axial' to 10 digits; with \(\Delta\Omega \propto s^2(1 - s^2)\) (degrees 0, 2, 4), \(\psi\) is rebuilt from degrees 1–7 to \(4\cdot10^{-15}\), ferraro_mismatch is \(5\cdot10^{-14}\), and the budgets close to \(\le 2\cdot10^{-11}\) in a shell, a full sphere and 'Wu 2005'.

  • diff_rot_type = 'ferraro': the uniform axial field with \(F = \psi\) gives the eigenvalues of the cylindrical profile to 10 digits, and so does the round trip through B0 = 'ferraro' (\(G = 5w\); budgets \(4\cdot10^{-14}\)). Budgets \(\le 10^{-10}\) for all of the following, with ferraro_mismatch:

    field \(F\) ferraro_mismatch 'FDM' \(\psi\) \(3\cdot10^{-12}\) 'G21 dipole', 'Luo_S1' \(\psi\) \(6\cdot10^{-12}\) full sphere \(\psi\) \(2\cdot10^{-12}\) 'general', degrees 1 + 3 \(\psi + \psi^2\) \(2\cdot10^{-11}\) 'Luo_S2' \(\psi^2\) \(2\cdot10^{-10}\) 'confined', cut at diff_rot_nmax 4 \(\psi\) \(7\cdot10^{-9}\)

    Refused as they should be: an odd \(F\) with 'Luo_S2', B0 = 'ferraro', a toroidal field alone, a conducting inner core with \(\psi\) not constant on it. With a toroidal part of degree 2: B0 = 'ferraro' + 'Malkus' and 'Luo_S1' + 'wall' with diff_rot_type = 'ferraro' close their budgets to \(8\cdot10^{-12}\) and \(10^{-9}\).

  • B0_wound = 1 (tests/magnetic/wound_check.py): a uniform axial \(\mathbf B_p\) with \(\Delta\Omega = a r^2\) gives one degree, \(k_2 = A r^4/14 + C r^2 + D r^{-3}\): the solution matches it to \(7\cdot10^{-14}\) (shell), \(4\cdot10^{-13}\) (conducting inner core) and \(3\cdot10^{-12}\) (full sphere). The residual of the steady induction equation, by finite differences in \((r, \theta)\) with \(\mathbf B_p\) from its flux function, is \(\le 8\cdot10^{-10}\) ('general' 1 + 3, 'Luo_S2' in a full sphere, 'FDM' with a conducting inner core), the floor of the differences; the \(k_n\) change by \(\le 2\cdot10^{-11}\) from 97 to 385 nodes. Budgets with the ratio of the maxima of the wound and the poloidal field from 0.5 to 4.4 ('general', 'FDM' with a conducting inner core, 'Luo_S2' in a full sphere, 'axial' plus a 'Malkus' part of degree 2): \(\le 2.4\cdot10^{-10}\).

  • Unchanged without the new features: regress.sh bitwise, heat_dr, ru_insane identical, and 26 magnetic cases build A and B bitwise equal to the code before.

docs.title: Free decay without the flow (2026-11-06)
docs.text:
Without the flow (hydro = 0, as conductive_IC) a field of uniform conductivity only diffuses, and each mode decays at the rate MagnetD \(k^2\), where \(k\) makes the spherical Bessel functions \(j_l(kr)\), \(y_l(kr)\) meet the conditions at the walls: \(j_{l-1}(k)\,y_{l+1}(kr_i) = y_{l-1}(k)\,j_{l+1}(kr_i)\) for a poloidal field between insulators, \(j_l(k)\,y_l(kr_i) = y_l(k)\,j_l(kr_i)\) for a toroidal one, and a 3 × 3 determinant with \(j_l(k\sqrt{\sigma_{i2o}}\,r)\) inside a conducting inner core. tests/decay/decay_check.py finds the roots with scipy and compares (ricb = 0.35, N 48, lmax 15, m 0, MagnetD 1):

case modes largest relative error resid𝐛, resid𝐄 insulating walls poloidal \(l\) = 1 (two), 3; toroidal \(l\) = 2: rates 10.041029, 45.156235, 33.260470, 37.495006 4e-15 ≤ 5e-12 conducting inner core, sigma_i2o 0.3 the same: 9.993017, 43.759526, 33.248628, 35.942816 6e-14 ≤ 8e-11 full sphere \(\pi^2\), \(4\pi^2\), and 33.217462 (poloidal \(l\) = 3 and toroidal \(l\) = 2 together) 9e-15 ≤ 2e-13

With a differential rotation the modes of the field alone equal, to \(10^{-15}\), those of the same run with the flow and a B0 of \(10^{-9}\), where the field and the flow decouple; the entropy of 'Boussinesq' decays at the exact rates too, and the field of just_induction.py with solve_ind.py is that of a mode without Lorentz force to \(10^{-14}\).

docs.title: Thin conducting layer (2026-11-06)
docs.text:
The thin layers were ported from conductive_IC (2d84351) and checked against exact decay rates, against that branch, and with the energy budgets (tests/twa/twa_check.py).

Free decay. Without the flow each mode decays at MagnetD \(k^2\), where \(k\) makes \(j_l(kr)\), \(y_l(kr)\) meet the thin-wall conditions with \(\mathcal D_l F = -k^2 F\) (ricb 0.35, N 48, m 0, MagnetD 1; poloidal \(l\) = 1 (two modes), 3 and toroidal \(l\) = 2):

walls largest relative error resid𝐄 outer, \(c = 0\), \(c_1 = 0.1\) 9e-16 8e-14 outer, \(c = 0.05\), \(c_1 = 0.1\), \(p\) = 1, 3, \(\infty\) 4e-15 2e-2 to 3e-2 inner, \(c = 0\), \(c_1 = 0.2\) 2e-15 4e-14 both, \(\mu\) = 1.5 2e-15 nan full sphere, \(c = 0.05\), \(c_1 = 0.1\), \(p\) = 2, 3 3e-15 2e-2

With \(c \neq 0\) resid𝐄 scales as \(c\,c_1\) (at \(c\,c_1 = 5\cdot10^{-5}\): \(2\cdot10^{-5}\) to \(5\cdot10^{-4}\) whether \(c\) or \(c_1\) is the larger), at or below \(\varepsilon_\text{TWA}\); the toroidal modes close to round-off (their condition has no \(c\)).

Against conductive_IC. Thirteen runs with the flow ('Boussinesq', Ek, Em and Le² \(10^{-3}\), N 48, lmax 19 to 21): no-slip and stress-free walls, a thin layer at either or both boundaries, \(p\) = 1, 2, 3, 4 and \(\infty\), \(\mu\) = 1.3, the fields 'axial', 'G21 dipole', 'Luo_S2' and 'FDM', \(m\) = 0, 1, 2, both equatorial symmetries, and a full sphere. The eigenvalues agree to \(3\cdot10^{-14}\), resid𝐄 and εTWA to the printed digits, and the energies and losses of the budget (MEic, E_w, MEext, Ohm_w, relative to Ohm_f) to about \(10^{-10}\).

Budgets. With a slipping fluid and \(c = 0\), resid𝐄 closes to about \(10^{-10}\) (N 48), and with 'Wu 2005' (r_out 0.9, N 96, lmax 40) to \(2.5\cdot10^{-10}\), as for insulating walls. A rigid rotation offset (diff_rot_type = 'rigid', \(a\) = 0.3, thin layers with \(c \neq 0\) and a slipping fluid) gives the eigenvalues of the frame turning with the solids to \(6\cdot10^{-15}\), with resid𝐄 and εTWA unchanged. With walls turning at different rates ('shellular_boussinesq') resid𝐄 closes to \(3\cdot10^{-10}\), and for a conducting inner core turning with the fluid it went from \(1.5\cdot10^{-4}\) to \(5\cdot10^{-10}\) (INDU_ROT_SOLID, above).

docs.title: Resolved conducting mantle (2026-11-06)
docs.text:
The resolved mantle was ported from conductive_IC (2d84351) and checked against exact decay rates, against that branch, against the thin layer, and with the energy budgets (tests/mantle/mantle_check.py).

Free decay. Without the flow each mode decays at MagnetD \(k^2\), with \(j_l(kr)\), \(y_l(kr)\) in the fluid and in the layer \(j_l(k\sqrt\sigma\,r)\), \(y_l(k\sqrt\sigma\,r)\) for a uniform \(\sigma\), or the solution of its equations integrated from \(r_s\) (scipy's DOP853 at rtol \(10^{-13}\)), matched as above (ricb 0.35, N 48, m 0, MagnetD 1; poloidal \(l\) = 1 (two modes), 3 and toroidal \(l\) = 2):

layer rates largest relative error resid𝐛, resid𝐄 \(\sigma\) = 0.3, \(r_s\) = 1.4 (conductive_IC's test) 8.220477, 33.204363, 29.002791, 28.121940 1e-15 ≤ 1e-13 \(\sigma = 0.3\,e^{-10(r-1)}\), \(r_s\) = 1.4 (conductive_IC's test) 9.521791, 42.322149, 31.916490, 34.954516 7e-15 ≤ 8e-13 full sphere, \(\sigma\) = 2, \(r_s\) = 1.3 3.790859, 19.320734, 11.729515, 15.398290 1e-15 ≤ 6e-13 conducting inner core (sigma_i2o 0.3), \(\sigma = 0.5\,r^{-6}\), \(r_s\) = 1.5 8.623323, 36.247125, 29.781714, 29.597419 2e-14 ≤ 1e-12

Against conductive_IC. Five runs with the flow ('Boussinesq', Ek, Em and Le² \(10^{-3}\), N 48, lmax 19 to 21): no-slip walls under a uniform layer, a fluid slipping along both walls with a field of degree 2 under an exponential layer, a full sphere with a slipping fluid, a conducting inner core, and \(m\) = 2 under a thin layer (\(r_s\) = 1.1, \(\sigma\) = 2) with a slipping fluid. The eigenvalues agree to \(7\cdot10^{-15}\), resid𝐄 to the printed digits, and the energies and losses of the budget (E_w, Ohm_w, MEext, relative to Ohm_f) to about \(10^{-10}\).

Limits. A layer of thickness \(h\) and conductance \(\sigma h\) = 0.01, with a fluid slipping along it, differs from the thin layer with \(c = h\) and \(c_1\) = 0.01 by \(1.0\cdot10^{-4}\), \(5.2\cdot10^{-5}\) and \(2.6\cdot10^{-5}\) for \(h\) = 0.01, 0.005 and 0.0025: at first order in \(h\). A layer of \(\sigma = 10^{-9}\) gives the eigenvalues of an insulating mantle to \(3\cdot10^{-12}\).

Budgets and rotation. With 'Wu 2005' (r_out 0.9, N 64), a conducting inner core and a fluid slipping along an exponential layer, a rigid rotation offset (\(a\) = 0.3) gives the eigenvalues of the frame turning with the solids to \(3\cdot10^{-15}\), with resid𝐄 \(2.5\cdot10^{-10}\) in both frames, and with the layer, the inner core and the fluid turning at different rates (\(\Delta\Omega = 0.4\,(0.5 + r^2)\)) resid𝐄 closes to \(3\cdot10^{-10}\). The field of just_induction.py with solve_ind.py is that of a mode without Lorentz force to \(4\cdot10^{-14}\), in the fluid and in the layer.

docs.title: Forced runs (2026-11-06)
docs.text:
The forced runs with a field were ported from conductive_IC (2d84351) and checked against that branch, against the Chebyshev inner core, with exact identities of the matrices, with the energy budgets, and with the limit of a thin resolved mantle (tests/forced_field/forced_check.py; 'Boussinesq', Ek, Em and Le² \(10^{-3}\), N 48 unless stated).

Against conductive_IC. Eight runs: libration (\(m\) = 0) with insulating, conducting (Chebyshev and Bessel) and thin-layer inner cores, thin-layer and resolved mantles, and the fields 'axial' and 'Luo_S2'; forcing 9 with insulating walls, and with thin layers under 'deforming'. The kinetic energy and the magnetic energies in the fluid and in the inner core agree to the 10 digits written, and resid𝐄 closes to \(1.4\cdot10^{-14}\) to \(6\cdot10^{-10}\). A conducting inner core behind a wall that moves radially is not compared: conductive_IC follows neither picture there.

Bessel and Chebyshev. With the core at rest ('rigid'), under forcing 9, also with the core turning with a differential rotation ('shellular_boussinesq', N 64) and with a core of conductivity 0.3 times the fluid's, and with one of conductivity 0.3 and permeability 1.5 times the fluid's where the forcing moves the outer wall only, and under forcing 6, 'conducting, Bessel' gives the flow and the field of 'conducting, Chebys' (N_cic 32, 40 with the rotation) to \(4.4\cdot10^{-14}\), and the core's energy and Ohmic loss to the 10 digits written. \(x_d\) agrees with mpmath (50 digits) to \(5\cdot10^{-13}\) for \(l\) up to 300 and \(\lvert x\rvert\) up to \(1.4\cdot10^4\).

Matrices. Two forcing frequencies give matrices that differ by \(i\,\Delta w\,B\) to \(1.4\cdot10^{-16}\), and frequency 0 gives the eigenproblem's \(A\) exactly, with a conducting inner core under the resolved mantle and with a thin layer at the outer wall and \(\mu_{i2o}\) = 2. A frequency scan of forcing 11 with a conducting inner core gives the same spectrum whether \(A\) was assembled at 0.3 or 0.5. The couplings of \(u_r\hat{\mathbf r}\times\mathbf B_0\) (assemble.bc_b_radial) agree with a projection on a Gauss grid to \(10^{-15}\), for a poloidal field of degrees 1 and 3 and a toroidal one of degrees 2 and 4, at both walls, and with half the toroidal part alone.

Budgets with the solids at rest ('rigid'). resid𝐄 closes where the walls move: with 'Wu 2005' (r_out 0.9, N 96) under forcing 9 with the Bessel core (\(1.3\cdot10^{-10}\)) and forcing 14 with a thin outer layer (\(1.2\cdot10^{-11}\)); with a toroidal \(\mathbf B_0\) ('Malkus', not zero at the walls) under forcing 9 with thin layers (\(6\cdot10^{-14}\)) and under the resolved mantle (\(10^{-15}\)); forcing 10 with a thin outer layer (\(10^{-12}\)); a full sphere (N 96) under forcing 9 with a thin outer layer (\(5\cdot10^{-13}\); \(10^{-7}\) at N 48, as a full sphere needs about twice the N of a shell); forcing 9 under the resolved mantle with the Chebyshev core (\(1.5\cdot10^{-10}\)), also with a fluid slipping along the mantle (\(1.9\cdot10^{-10}\)); forcing 7 with \(m\) = 2 under the resolved mantle with the Bessel core (\(10^{-12}\)); forcing 6 through a slipping thin inner layer (\(2\cdot10^{-17}\)), and through a no-slip one while a thin outer layer of permeability 2 that does not conduct stays in place (\(6\cdot10^{-15}\)). Where no wall moves radially it closes as well, with 'Wu 2005': forcing 13 with the Chebyshev core (\(5\cdot10^{-10}\)), and libration under the resolved mantle (\(1.6\cdot10^{-14}\)). With 'Wu 2005' it needs the radial resolution: \(6\cdot10^{-7}\) at N 64, \(1.3\cdot10^{-10}\) at 96 and \(2\cdot10^{-14}\) at 128. In eigenvalue problems with a free wall (bco or bci 2) the magnetic pressure took residσ from \(7\cdot10^{-4}\) to \(10^{-2}\) down to below \(10^{-10}\), and resid𝐄, not computed there before, closes to \(8\cdot10^{-11}\).

Budgets with deforming solids ('deforming'). resid𝐄 closes under forcing 14 with thin layers (\(2.4\cdot10^{-12}\)), and with the resolved mantle and the Chebyshev core deforming: forcings 9 and 14 with 'Wu 2005' (\(3.4\cdot10^{-12}\), \(1.1\cdot10^{-10}\)); forcing 9 with 'G21 dipole' (\(1.2\cdot10^{-10}\)), also with a fluid slipping along the mantle (\(2.2\cdot10^{-10}\)) and with a core of conductivity 0.3 times the fluid's (\(1.4\cdot10^{-10}\)), and with the mantle alone, of conductivity \(0.5\,e^{-5(r-1)}\) (\(2\cdot10^{-11}\)) and in a full sphere (N 96, \(3\cdot10^{-10}\)); with 'Malkus' (\(8.5\cdot10^{-14}\), and \(3.9\cdot10^{-14}\) with thin layers), 'Luo_S2' (\(1.7\cdot10^{-10}\)) and a 'general' field of poloidal degrees 1, 3 and toroidal 2, 4 (\(1.6\cdot10^{-12}\), and \(9\cdot10^{-13}\) with thin layers); forcings 6, 10 and 7 with \(m\) = 2 (\(6\cdot10^{-14}\), \(10^{-14}\), \(1.1\cdot10^{-10}\)); and with the differential rotation (N 64, \(2.3\cdot10^{-10}\)). Without the work of the solids' motion resid𝐄 is \(8.6\cdot10^{-2}\) ('G21 dipole'), \(2.5\cdot10^{-2}\) ('Wu 2005') and \(1.4\cdot10^{-2}\) ('Malkus'), and without the half toroidal field of a deforming thin layer \(2.1\cdot10^{-2}\) ('Malkus').

A thin resolved mantle. A mantle of thickness \(h\) and conductivity \(0.02/h\) under forcing 9 at the outer wall tends to the thin layer of conductance 0.02 at first order in \(h\), in both pictures. Its field differs from that of the thin layer by \(1.1\cdot10^{-2}\) and \(5.6\cdot10^{-3}\) for \(h\) = 0.01 and 0.005 with 'axial' at rest, by \(4.6\cdot10^{-3}\), \(2.3\cdot10^{-3}\) and \(1.15\cdot10^{-3}\) for \(h\) = 0.01, 0.005 and 0.0025 deforming, and with 'Malkus' by \(2.0\cdot10^{-2}\) and \(1.0\cdot10^{-2}\) at rest, \(1.9\cdot10^{-2}\), \(9.6\cdot10^{-3}\) and \(4.8\cdot10^{-3}\) deforming. A deforming mantle moves across the drop of 'Malkus' to zero at \(r_s\): without the half toroidal field in the thin layer's conditions (background.thin_drop) the difference stayed at 78% for every \(h\).

Kinematic induction. just_induction.py and solve_ind.py give back the field of the coupled run from its flow, to \(4\cdot10^{-15}\), with the Bessel core, under the resolved mantle, and with both solids deforming.

docs.title: Dipole and slipping inner core (2026-11-07)
docs.text:
B0 = 'dipole' and a fluid slipping along a conducting inner core were ported from conductive_IC (2d84351) and checked against that branch, between the two cores, and with the energy budgets (tests/inner_core/core_check.py; 'Boussinesq', N 48).

The dipole. Seven eigenvalue runs (Ek \(10^{-3}\), Em = Le = \(10^{-2}\), cnorm 1): insulating walls, cnorm = 'mag_energy', the antisymmetric modes, a thin layer at the outer wall, the resolved mantle, a thin layer on the inner core, and the rotating solids with a conducting inner core. The eigenvalues agree with conductive_IC to \(4\cdot10^{-12}\) (its \(r^{-2}\) series of \(h\) is cut at tol_B0), and resid𝐋 closes to \(2\cdot10^{-12}\). The libration of the mantle with the Bessel core gives its kinetic energy to the 10 digits written.

A slipping inner wall. Five eigenvalue runs with bci = 0 and 'conducting, Chebys' (Ek, Em and Le² \(10^{-3}\), or Em = Le = \(10^{-2}\) with the dipole): 'axial' with the antisymmetric modes of \(m\) = 1 and with \(m\) = 0, the dipole, 'G21 dipole' with \(\mu_{i2o}\) = 2 and \(\sigma_{i2o}\) = 0.3, and 'Luo_S2' with both walls stress-free and \(\sigma_{i2o}\) = 0.5. The eigenvalues agree with conductive_IC to \(6\cdot10^{-13}\) (\(4\cdot10^{-15}\) without the dipole), resid𝐄 closes to \(2\cdot10^{-11}\) and resid𝐋 (\(m\) = 0) to \(3\cdot10^{-15}\). Without the slip's term in the core's row resid𝐄 is \(7\cdot10^{-5}\) to \(4\cdot10^{-2}\), while resid𝐛, the budget of the fluid alone, does not see it. With 'Wu 2005' (r_out 0.9, N 96, N_cic 48, with buoyancy) resid𝐄 closes to \(4\cdot10^{-10}\) (\(2\cdot10^{-8}\) in the most damped mode with N_cic 24); the slip's term in \((\ln\rho_0)'\) acts only where the flow crosses the wall, under forcing 6 (below). A rigid rotation offset (diff_rot_type = 'rigid', \(a\) = 0.3, both walls stress-free) gives the eigenvalues of the frame turning with the solids to \(2\cdot10^{-14}\), with the same resid𝐄, and just_induction.py with solve_ind.py gives back the field of a mode without Lorentz force, in the fluid and in the core, to \(6\cdot10^{-15}\).

Forced runs. The libration of the mantle with a slipping inner wall, with 'axial' and with the dipole: both cores give conductive_IC's kinetic energy to the 10 digits written, and the same flow and field to \(3\cdot10^{-14}\). Forcing 10 with 'G21 dipole', \(\sigma_{i2o}\) = 0.3 and \(\mu_{i2o}\) = 1.5, which a wrong factor of either would show: the Bessel core gives the Chebyshev one to \(2\cdot10^{-14}\), as it does under forcing 6, which moves the inner wall past the core at rest, and under forcing 10 with a differential rotation ('shellular_boussinesq', N 64). resid𝐄 closes to \(4\cdot10^{-10}\) in all, and under forcing 6 with the core deforming, with 'axial' and with the dipole, which the deforming core holds as \(a\,x + b\,x^3\) (\(6\cdot10^{-11}\)). Forcing 6 in 'Wu 2005' closes it to \(6\cdot10^{-12}\), and to \(2\cdot10^{-3}\) only without the slip's term in \((\ln\rho_0)'\).

Stops. A toroidal \(\mathbf B_0\) that is not zero at the wall of an inviscid full sphere with an insulator beyond stops the run (Current sheets at slipping walls), also where it is \(4\cdot10^{-6}\) of the field under a strong 'axial' one, and where a profile that is not smooth at the centre misses its zero at the wall (the message says so); with rotdyn = 1 it stops at any wall. At a viscous slipping wall the run goes on, the push in its stress rows: stress-free outer and inner walls (bco or bci 0 or 2) and a thin layer that does not conduct, at either wall. So it does with no-slip walls, a conducting inner core, a conducting thin layer, the resolved mantle or 'wall'. 'general' and 'user' profiles that are not finite where they are interpolated (r = 0 in a full sphere) stop too, and so does a field that is zero, which 'mag_energy' cannot normalise ('ferraro' among them), or a 'ferraro' field that is not finite.

docs.title: Current sheets at slipping walls (2026-11-07)
docs.text:
tests/sheet/sheet_check.py (run_all.sh, about 11 min on 2 ranks) checks the push of the sheets (Current sheets at slipping walls) with Ek = Em = \(10^{-2}\), Hendrik 0.1, N 160, \(m\) = 1, 'Boussinesq' unless stated.

Smoothed sheets. A sheet is the limit of a field that falls to the field beyond across a thin layer in the fluid, whose force kore takes in the volume. With layers of width \(\delta\) = \(2\cdot10^{-3}\), \(10^{-3}\) and \(5\cdot10^{-4}\), the first four eigenvalues of the run with the sheet and its push are approached as \(\delta\) (the error halves with \(\delta\), by 0.49 to 0.53), and the extrapolation to \(\delta = 0\) that removes the terms in \(\delta\) and \(\delta^2\) meets them to \(8\cdot10^{-8}\) to \(5\cdot10^{-5}\), against \(9\cdot10^{-3}\) to 1.7 for the run without the push. Nine cases: a toroidal sheet (\(k = r\)) at the outer wall and at an inner wall with zero radial stress (bci = 2, with cnorm_tor 2 and Hendrik 0.025, which give the eigenvalues of 1 and 0.1 to \(10^{-13}\), so that a push that missed the normalisation would show); a poloidal one ('general') at the outer wall (degrees 1 and 3, cnorm 2 and Hendrik 0.025) and at the inner one; at an outer thin layer that does not conduct (\(c\) = 0.05, \(p\) = 3, \(\mu\) = 1.5) and at an inner one, with degree 3 (\(\mu\) = 0.8), which bring in the terms \(e\); the toroidal sheet at the outer wall of 'Wu 2005' (r_out 0.9) with a viscosity \(1 + r\), where \( ho_0 u\) is 0.07 at the wall; the outer toroidal sheet with a drag at the same wall (kappa_cmb 0.01), whose terms share its rows and which moves the eigenvalues by \(2\cdot10^{-2}\); and a poloidal and a toroidal sheet together at the outer wall with \(m\) = 2 and symm = -1, whose rows and columns are the other sets of degrees.

Angular momentum. With \(m\) = 0 between insulating stress-free walls nothing outside the fluid exerts a torque on it, so a mode with \(\lambda eq 0\) carries no axial angular momentum \(L_z\). With a toroidal sheet of degree 2 at the walls under 'axial' (N 64; 96 for 'Wu 2005'), \(\lvert L_z vert\) is below \(10^{-13}\) in a shell (with cnorm_tor = 'mag_energy'), a full sphere and 'Wu 2005' (0.6 to 1.1 without the push), and so is resid𝐋.

Budgets. residσ and resid𝐄 close to \(2\cdot10^{-10}\) in all these runs (resid𝐄 is nan with \(\mu eq 1\)).

Stops. The runs stop with their messages: an inviscid full sphere with a poloidal sheet, also behind a layer where the permeability jumps, where the message asks for a field that meets the layer's condition (with B0_cmb = 'wall' the same run goes on); centrifugal = 1 with a sheet at a slipping wall; and a field that goes on beyond a slipping wall where the permeability jumps: 'axial' with \(\mu\) = 1.5 or a thin layer with \(p\) = 2, at the outer wall, at the inner one and in an inviscid fluid, and 'dipole' and 'G21 dipole' with 'frozen currents' at the inner wall. With a no-slip wall or one permeability they go on, and so does a poloidal sheet at a wall with zero radial stress. The toroidal sheet's stops and runs are in tests/inner_core (above).

The walls' conditions. A poloidal sheet's drop comes from the steady condition of the wall (background._pol_wall_row), which the smoothed sheets cannot check: a wrong condition would leave a sheet in the smoothed runs too, which the push would then follow. Its rows equal the solver's (assemble.bc_b_spherical: an insulator's, or a thin layer's with \(c_1 = 0\)) at both walls, degrees 1 to 6, to \(2\cdot10^{-16}\), in the runs of the outer poloidal sheet and of the two thin layers. 'FDM' and 'G21 dipole', which B0_cmb = 'wall' adjusts to an outer layer where the permeability jumps, have no sheet there, while 'G21 dipole' with B0_cmb = 'plain' has one.

Interpolated profiles. The profiles of 'general', 'ferraro' and B0_tor = 'user', the wound field's \(\Delta\Omega\) and the resolved mantle's \(\ln\sigma\) are Chebyshev interpolants whose coefficients come from a DCT since 2026-11-07. numpy's interpolation, used before, left round-off that grows with the degree, above the cut at \(10^{-13}\) from N about 450, and the derivatives at the walls amplified it: with a 'general' field \(h_1 = r^2\) (no-slip walls, Ek \(10^{-3}\)) the eigenvalues moved by \(3\cdot10^{-5}\) at N 450 and \(2\cdot10^{-4}\) at N 800, and the operators filled up in \(r\). They now agree to \(10^{-13}\) from N 160 to 800. A B0_tor = 'user' profile also kept the round-off of its interpolant, unlike 'general': it moved the eigenvalues with N (\(10^{-8}\) at N 240) and left residσ at \(10^{-4}\) where the fluid crosses the wall (bci = 2). So did the wound field's \(\Delta\Omega\), whose slope its source takes (a slope of \(2\cdot10^{-4}\) of itself at N 800 for the 'conical' rotation, constant in \(r\)), and the wound field itself, cut at \(10^{-14}\) (its second derivative, the highest that the operators take, \(2\cdot10^{-7}\) of its largest value off at the walls at N 800): both are now cut at \(10^{-13}\).
